title: Do Models Refuse the Same Prompts? Mapping the Shared Refusal Boundary

original_idea.body:
# Do Models Refuse the Same Prompts? Mapping the Shared Refusal Boundary

**Problem:** Models share internal refusal directions, implying refusal BEHAVIOR may be correlated. On borderline prompts, do independent models refuse/comply in lockstep?

**Direction:** Build a graded set of borderline prompts. Run ~10 open models, label each response refuse/partial/comply, and compute inter-model agreement at each graded level. Identify the correlated over- and under-refusal zones.

**Why it matters:** Correlated over-refusal hurts usefulness uniformly; correlated under-refusal means a single jailbreak class works everywhere.

**Relevant context:** Shared refusal representations (arXiv:2506.12913); correlated-failure framing.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (correlated under-refusal -> a jailbreak class works everywhere) with systemic framing, but a measurement step from mitigation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Behavioral refuse/comply labeling on graded prompts; accessible, no internals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped agreement measurement on a graded prompt set.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Behavioral, public models; correlated refusal-boundary auditing labs deprioritize.

novelty.reasoning: Shared refusal directions known; behavioral lockstep mapping partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Refusal-direction sharing known internally; behavioral cross-model boundary mapping less covered.
